clue.text: Current means of transport into club game

indicators.note: the current and the transport go into the club, so the club's letters wrap around them

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
AC is alternating current
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Someone takes an electric tram into a club to play some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts ACCAR inside BAT. 'club' looks like the gambling club of the surface but is the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos.

clue.text: He throws out the troublemaker with a dud cheque

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman ejects a troublemaker who has paid with a worthless cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text repeated 'troublemaker'; the page prints it once.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman ejects rowdy patrons; a cheque that bounces is returned unpaid by the bank.

clue.text: Senior officer with godliness in abundance

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
piously means in a godly or devout way

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer has religious devotion in large measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Copiously means plentifully, in large amounts.

clue.text: Absence of harmful bacteria-but one passes out!

definitions.text: Absence of harmful bacteria-but one passes out!

parts.words: Absence of harmful bacteria-but one passes out!
parts.note: split the word after its first letter and it becomes a blood infection that could make someone faint, the very opposite of germ-free

explanation.surface: Even with no germs about, someone still faints.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a plain definition of a germ-free state; the second plays on reading the word as A SEPSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the condition of being free of disease-causing microbes, as in a sterile operating theatre.

clue.text: Swelling appears to tax a surgeon at first

indicators.note: the article and the surgeon come before the tax in the answer

parts.note: BS is Bachelor of Surgery, a surgeon's degree
cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A rising bill seems to burden a surgeon from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: BS, Bachelor of Surgery, stands for a surgeon; 'appears to' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess is a painful pocket of pus that makes tissue puff up.

clue.text: Endlessly canoodle with sailor providing drink

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for canoodle is dropped

parts.note: to canoodle is to kiss and cuddle, to neck
TAR is a sailor, from tarpaulin

explanation.surface: A sailor, after a lot of cuddling, is handed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the K from NECK to leave NEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods, and loosely any delicious drink.

clue.text: Infamous in Bordeaux, we put in to port

indicators.note: the words for to and port are placed inside the French word

parts.note: nous is French for we, Bordeaux being in France
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Something scandalous in a French city: we called in at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIO goes inside NOUS. 'put in to port' reads as a nautical phrase but is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means well known for something bad, the same as having a wicked reputation.

clue.text: Like an uneasy, lying Head victim of a strike?

definitions.text: Like an uneasy, lying Head victim of a strike?

parts.words: Like an uneasy, lying Head victim of a strike?
parts.note: recalls Shakespeare's line about the head that wears royal regalia lying uneasy, and also a head hit hard on top

explanation.surface: A worried boss, perhaps a liar, is felled by industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry IV Part 2 has 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown'; to crown someone is also slang for hitting them on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's head wears a crown; a person struck on top of the skull has been hit on the crown.

clue.text: Where we may learn to identify a rebel vessel!

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht

explanation.surface: A school where pupils learn to recognise a mutinous ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade is a famous English rebel; MY is a motor yacht. 'to identify' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or place of training.

clue.text: But Mrs Warren's Profession isn't such a bad play!

definitions.text: But Mrs Warren's Profession isn't such a bad play!

parts.words: But Mrs Warren's Profession isn't such a bad play!
parts.note: Shaw grouped Mrs Warren's Profession among his three disagreeable dramas, against a companion volume of agreeable ones, so the play is not the opposite of nice

explanation.surface: A theatregoer defends Shaw's once-banned play about prostitution as not so bad after all.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw published Mrs Warren's Profession in his collection Plays Unpleasant, alongside Plays Pleasant; the clue says it is not a pleasant one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's own label for this group of plays was the opposite of pleasant.

clue.text: It's spoken in Ecuador all the time

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words Ecuador all

explanation.surface: A remark about a language spoken in Ecuador all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across ecuadOR ALl; 'the time' just finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oral is spoken rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Ill-humoured character directing us to another place

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered
a character is a written testimonial, also called a reference

explanation.surface: A grumpy person tells us to go somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is not a person but a testimonial from an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-reference in a book points the reader to another entry or page.

clue.text: Lives in lodgings, but refuses to comply

indicators.note: the word for lives goes into the word for lodgings

parts.note: a rest is an old word for a place to lodge or stop
lives in the sense of exists, as in he is

explanation.surface: A lodger lives in rented rooms but won't obey the house rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' is a verb here, exists, not the plural noun; a rest is an old word for a lodging place.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or refuse to give way to something.

clue.text: Evidence upset Athenian youth leader

parts.note: read as set put up, the word set turned upwards in a down clue
Timon of Athens, the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: Testimony upset a young leader from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is split as up + set: SET read upwards gives TES. Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthrope.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is a formal statement given as proof, especially in court.

clue.text: A bargain spoken of for so long

indicators.note: the phrase for a bargain is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: A bargain was talked about for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length of time but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal farewell, the same as saying cheerio.

clue.text: Writer seizes dishonourable fellow in bar

indicators.note: the writer's name grabs hold of the word for a rotter, taking it inside

parts.note: J M Barrie, author of Peter Pan
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: An author grabs a scoundrel in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan. 'bar' looks like a pub but is a blocking obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier set up to block passage.

clue.text: Moving ceremonial in smart person's earlier days

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
a person's past is their earlier life

explanation.surface: A ceremony recalls the good old days of a clever person.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY means shrewd in British slang. 'Moving' describes aircraft in motion, not emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-past is a ceremonial flight of aircraft in formation over a parade or event.

clue.text: Latvian salad ingredient named by a drunkard?

indicators.note: the salad leaf is said aloud in a slurred way, the way someone tipsy would mispronounce it

parts.note: lettuce is a salad leaf

explanation.surface: A tipsy man trying to say what's in a Latvian salad.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk's slurred 'lettuce' comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is an old name for the Latvian language or people.

clue.text: Question relatives supplying plant

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them for information
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Asking the family where a plant came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is a trailing gourd plant with large orange fruit.

clue.text: Oriental thus accepting role of a grass

parts.note: E for East, so oriental

indicators.note: the word for thus takes in the word for role, wrapping round it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: An Asian actor accepts the role of an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental' is the compass point East, not a person; 'grass' looks like an informer but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass from Spain and North Africa used to make rope and paper.

clue.text: In the heart of Greece, sports official turned recluse

indicators.note: the reversed official goes into the middle letters of Greece
the heart of the word Greece is its central pair of letters
the official's title is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a timer, or timekeeper, officiates at races

explanation.surface: A Greek sports official retired from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the official to give REMIT, which sits inside the central pair of letters of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit living alone.

clue.text: Series of actions resulting in a summons

explanation.surface: A sequence of events ends with someone being called to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a sequence of steps; in law, a process is a writ ordering someone to appear in court.

clue.text: Cotton product distributed from a Dee silo

indicators.note: the letters of Dee silo are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cotton waste is spread from a storage tower by the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges DEESILO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton seed is pressed for its oil, making it one example of an oil-bearing seed.

clue.text: Sentence originally introducing Macaulay's record of the distant past

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words introducing and Macaulay's are taken

parts.note: a memorial is a record kept in memory of something

explanation.surface: A line that begins one of the historian Macaulay's accounts of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives I and M. Lord Macaulay was a Victorian historian, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: From time immemorial means from a time so long ago that nobody remembers it.

clue.text: Deliberately provoke the elite

explanation.surface: Someone goads the upper classes on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick a fight is to start one on purpose; the pick of a group is its best members.

clue.text: Erase outside broadcast by educated person

parts.note: a literate is an educated person, one who can read and write

explanation.surface: A clever person wipes out an outdoor TV transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: LITERATE as a noun means an educated person.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, so to rub away.

clue.text: It's sung in a crudely built cabin

explanation.surface: Someone sings in a roughly made hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a sailors' work song; a shanty is also a rough shack.

clue.text: County fellow without a supporter in retirement

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the name wraps round the letter

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man from the shires lacks someone to look after him in his old age.
explanation.walkthrough: TED goes outside A to make TEAD. 'retirement' is going to bed, not leaving work; 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's frame holds a sleeper up when they turn in for the night.
